messages.subject: stack and group models
parts:
I am struggling with how to specify stack when having a spatio-temporal term like

f(position,model="rw1",group=station,
              control.group=list(model="besag",graph=cmat))
or
f(station="besag",graph=cmat,group=station,
              control.group=list(model="rw1"))

(by the way, is one of the two specifications better than the other when time series is long and number of stations is not that large?)

When I try to specify a stack, I do not know where to put the group variable (it does not seem that it would fit into data or effects parts but it has to be specified somehow ...).
I know that when the spatial part is given by spde, inla.spde.make.A and inla.spde.make.index will take care about the group spatial structure nicely, but how to proceed when this is not the case?

All the Best
 Marek

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] stack and group models
parts:
Hi,

Your example f()-specifications are a ibt messed up with regards to the indices, but for the model structure itself I'd go with the second of the two f()-alternatives;
Not all models can be used as group models, and having the more complex spatial model as the "main" model is the usual approach;
f(location, model = "besag", graph=cmat, group = time, control.group=list(model="rw1"))

For the stack, all inla.spde.make.index does is to create a list with one vector element for the "main" index and one vector for the "group" index (and one for the "replicate" aspect of the model, but that's not involved in this case) that gives the indexing to the entire model. The inla.spde.make.A() matrix then links that full model component to the individual observations.
For a besag+rw1 model, you probably already have the needed vectors for the observations; one pointing to the graph nodes and one with the time values, so just specify those in the "effects" part of the stack, together with an identity matrix for A;
something like A = list(1), effects = list(list(location=station, time = time))

Finn
